title: Close the interrupter: match the opening comma
subtitle: Boundaries · 28 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **28 of the official questions in Boundaries are this one** — 5 Easy, 15 Medium, 8 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- Earlier in the sentence, just before the blank, you see an opening comma or dash that starts an extra descriptive phrase (an appositive, a participial phrase, an introductory modifier).
- The choices differ in whether a closing comma appears at the blank, and sometimes in whether commas are scattered inside the phrase.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Find where the extra, removable information starts and ends.
- 2) Close it with the same mark that opened it: a comma for a comma, a dash for a dash.
- For an introductory phrase, put one comma where it hands off to the main subject.
- 3) Remove no commas inside the phrase, and add none there.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You leave the interrupter unclosed, or you add 'and' so that it reads as if two things are being joined.
You might also sprinkle commas inside the phrase, or close it with a different mark than the one that opened it.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You leave the interrupter unclosed, or you add 'and' so that it reads as if two things are being joined.
You might also sprinkle commas inside the phrase, or close it with a different mark than the one that opened it.
